company_news.headline: Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
company_news.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%. Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves. Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

company_news.headline: Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDA. Why Apple, Broadcom, and Anthropic Could Be Under Pressure
company_news.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) sent stocks sharply higher on Monday morning. NVIDIA shares opened up 34% at about $170, restoring more than $1 trillion of value to shareholders. The NASDAQ rose about 6.75% and the S&P 500 about 4.6%, erasing much of Friday's sell-off. Bleeker focuses on stocks lagging a market where nearly everything is up. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained only about 1.7%, and he says a rotation back into AI-adjacent names could pull capital out of the safe-haven stock. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) rose about 6% at the open, trailing the NASDAQ and semiconductor indexes. It fell about 12% Friday on reports that Google was cutting some of its TPU allocation. Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) also rose 6%, but its shares have been under pressure since Thursday's IPO, and NVIDIA's backing of open-weight models is a competitive threat. CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 5% at the open, partly on its $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS). Bleeker notes that money that moved into cybersecurity as semiconductors sold off could rotate back. He says to watch for competitive pressure on these names in the coming weeks.
